history.summary: The Maa Tarini Temple on Panposh Road, Civil Township, Rourkela (Sundargarh district) is a local Hindu shrine described as one of the oldest temples of Rourkela; its founding date and patron are UNVERIFIED. NOTE: this is NOT the famous Maa Tarini temple at Ghatagaon (Keonjhar district) nor the Tara Tarini temple of Ganjam district - those are distinct, far larger shrines; identity ambiguity flagged because several 'Maa Tarini Temple' listings exist in Rourkela. Coordinates are for the Panposh Road temple (geocoded full-address match).

name: Maa Tarini Temple
town_description: Rourkela is Odisha's second-largest city and its industrial capital, built around the Rourkela Steel Plant set up in the 1950s with German collaboration. It sits on the banks of the Brahmani river in Sundargarh district, near the Ib valley coalfields and the Khandadhar waterfalls. The city is known as the 'Steel City of Odisha' and serves as the main gateway for western Odisha's tribal hinterland.

travel.airport: Veer Surendra Sai Airport, Jharsuguda ~85 km (verify); Rourkela Airport (limited flights)
travel.road: On Panposh Road, Civil Township; city buses and autos serve the area
